properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — Anthony's idea, 2026-08-31, and this one questions the SHAPE of his own proposal rather than its content. Nothing chosen.

HE PROPOSED WALKING SUBSYSTEM BY SUBSYSTEM. The design has 18 Components at `level: subsystem`. Three things measured today suggest that unit may not bound the work:

· THE COUPLING IS A LEVEL DOWN. `detect_defects` reports coupling_by_level:
      component   86 components,  93 coupled pairs
      subsystem   18 components,   8 coupled pairs
      system       2 components,   0 coupled pairs
      part         2 components,   0 coupled pairs
  Nearly all the coupling is between COMPONENTS. A sweep bounded at subsystem level is mostly sweeping inside units that are not where the entanglement lives.

· THE SUBSYSTEMS ARE GROUPINGS, NOT BLACK BOXES — `fact:the-eight-subsystems-are-groupings-not-black-boxes` says so directly. A grouping does not give a boundary you can finish and move past.

· THE COARSE FILES CUT ACROSS ANYWAY. The five artifacts `granularity_report` names sit in two different crates and serve capabilities from several subsystems; `art:service` alone realizes 10. Working subsystem-by-subsystem would meet service.rs repeatedly, from several directions, and never as a whole.

OPTIONS, none chosen:
① BY SUBSYSTEM, as proposed. Familiar SE traversal, gives a completion story, and the design already names the 18.
② BY ARTIFACT, worst-first — take the five coarse files, since they are where the design and build disagree most and they are already ranked.
③ BY CRATE — two of them, which matches how the compiler and the test suite are actually bounded.
④ NOT A SWEEP AT ALL — take only what a measurement flags, and accept "nothing here" where nothing is flagged.

⚠️ THE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENT TO MY OWN OBJECTION: a systematic traversal has a virtue the ranked ones lack — it TERMINATES, and it can say what it covered. A worst-first list never says when you are done, and "take only what is flagged" inherits every blind spot of the instruments, which the sibling questions show are substantial. If the goal is assurance of coverage rather than a fix count, ① is the one that delivers it.
properties.name: OPEN — is "subsystem by subsystem" the right traversal for a cleanup sweep, when the coupling sits a level below and the coarse files cut across?
properties.rationale: Recorded under the brainstorm discipline. Raised as a question rather than as a correction: the subsystem traversal is a reasonable SE instinct and the measurements above are a reason to check it, not a reason to overrule it. The counter-argument is recorded in the same node deliberately, because the coverage property of a systematic walk is real and the alternatives do not have it.
